1.9.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the regulation defines and lists forms of violence including “kekerasan seksual” and “eksploitasi” (Pasal 3 ayat (1)), and defines “Eksploitasi Terhadap Anak” as acts aimed at enabling others to obtain “manfaat ekonomi, seksual, sosial, atau juga politik” (Pasal 1 angka 16). It also defines “Kekerasan Seksual” to include forced sex “dengan orang lain untuk tujuan komersial” (Pasal 1 angka 14). However, the text does not explicitly mention “perbudakan seksual” (sexual slavery) or an equivalent concept (e.g., enslavement, trafficking into sexual servitude) as a distinct category. Given the indicator is specifically “Sexual slavery / exploitation,” the document supports sexual exploitation (especially of children) but not clearly sexual slavery; if the coding standard requires explicit sexual slavery or explicit sexual exploitation of women (not just children), the golden “Yes” is likely overstated for this specific indicator. The judge’s ‘No’ is consistent with the absence of explicit sexual slavery language.

2.4.evaluator_rationale: While the text mentions gender justice/equality and a gender-responsive budget, it does not specifically mention institutionalized gender mainstreaming or a dedicated gender mainstreaming working group to deliver VAW policies/programs.
